summary_paragraph: A man with a history of type 2 diabetes, end-stage renal disease with two kidney transplants, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, and obstructive sleep apnea was admitted for fatigue and shortness of breath due to acute on chronic heart failure with fluid overload. He was started on IV diuresis with Lasix, which was later transitioned to oral torsemide. His blood pressure was labile, prompting adjustments to his antihypertensive regimen, including the addition of clonidine and isosorbide mononitrate. A right heart catheterization confirmed elevated filling pressures, and a pulmonary artery monitoring device was temporarily inserted to guide management. His symptoms improved, and he was discharged home on optimized medical therapy with instructions to monitor weight, hold hydralazine if blood pressure dropped below 100/60, and follow up with nephrology and cardiology. Outpatient sleep study and repeat renal ultrasound were recommended.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic (congestive) heart failure
Hypertensive heart disease with heart failure
Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic nephropathy
Peripheral artery disease with left below knee amputation
